correctness.rationale: Since p∤d the Fermat curve is smooth. The coordinate square morphism restricted to C is finite and generically one-to-one (the only potential diagonal sign flips violate A+B+E=0 unless coordinates vanish). Factoring the symmetric quartic in X^d,Y^d,Z^d yields G(X²,Y²,Z²)=0, and pulling back a general dual line gives degree 2d; Gauss [X^(d−1):...] is Frobenius_q after square-normalization, hence inseparable degree q. Derivatives of G on the torus cannot vanish simultaneously because 2≠0; on axes singularities occur exactly where the other dth powers coincide, giving 3d points. Locally G=(V^d−1−U^d)^2−4U^d and the coordinate change is étale (p∤d), yielding unibranch cusp delta(d−1)/2. Gradient at square-image gives the bidual power map of exponent d−2; gcd(d,d−2)=1 plus generic torus ratio proves it separable birational, so degree d(d−2). Arithmetic genus independently matches total cusp delta.
residual_risks: Algebraic closure and odd p are essential, e>=1; no bidual singularity classification.
Finite checks over F9/F25 demonstrate examples only, not infinite-field proof.

value.rationale: Explicit singularity geometry and duality failure of a natural Fermat family in positive characteristic give a nontrivial complete geometric classification: equation, normalization, cusp analytic types, and sharply larger bidual degree. This can be used as a precise example in studying inseparable Gauss maps and nonreflexivity.
residual_risks: The general polar/Plücker degree framework is classical and not itself credited as an innovation.

limitations: Restricted to odd p and d=2p^e+1; bidual singularities and full iterated duals unproved.
